items.stem: All else equal, increasing financial gearing tends to:

options.text: Increase the volatility of returns to equity shareholders
options.rationale: Correct: higher gearing increases financial risk and the volatility of equity returns.
More debt raises, not reduces, financial risk.
Gearing does not remove the cost of equity.
There is no guarantee; gearing raises risk as well as potential return.

items.explanation: Correct: higher gearing increases financial risk and the volatility of equity returns.

items.stem: A project has a cost of capital of 10%, year-1 cash flow of 110 and no other flows, with an initial outlay of 100. Its NPV is:

options.rationale: 10 ignores discounting of the 110 cash flow.
The discounted inflow equals the outlay, so NPV is 0, not negative.
100 is the discounted inflow, not the net present value.

items.stem: Select TWO methods commonly used to value a business.

options.rationale: Correct: DCF values a business on the present value of future cash flows.

options.text: Comparable market multiples such as P/E
options.rationale: Correct: relative valuation using market multiples is a standard method.
Depreciation is an accounting allocation, not a valuation method.
The current ratio is a liquidity measure, not a valuation method.

options.text: The dividend declared last year alone
options.rationale: A single past dividend is not itself a valuation method.

items.explanation: Correct: DCF values a business on the present value of future cash flows.
